name: P2 · Unit 7 — Software Engineering
description: All topics so far (8 sets × 30 questions): Software Process Models; Agile Process Models; Software Requirements; Software Design; Software Testing. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

sets.name: 1 · Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle

questions.question: In the software generic process model, ____ executes the activities in a circular manner.
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Pressman: an evolutionary process flow executes the activities in a circular manner; an iterative flow repeats activities before moving on. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
In the software iterative process flow, mark the correct order and choose the correct answer
a. Planning
b. Communication
c. Construction
d. Modelling
e. Deployment
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Pressman's generic framework: communication → planning → modelling → construction → deployment. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question:
In the following phases of SDLC, choose the correct phases of SDLC
a. Maintenance phase
b. Design phase
c. Debugging phase
d. Requirement analysis phase

options.A: a, b, c and d are phases of SDLC
options.B: a, b and d are phases of SDLC
options.C: b, c and d are phases of SDLC
options.D: b and d are only phases of SDLC

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Debugging is an activity within coding/testing, not a separate SDLC phase. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of software development life cycle phases.
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Requirements first, then design, coding and testing. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q13

questions.question:
Arrange the following software processes in correct order.
(i) Detailed Design
(ii) Coding
(iii) Operation & Maintenance
(iv) Testing
(v) Feasibility Analysis
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Feasibility → design → coding → testing → operation and maintenance. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question:
Examine the following statements and choose the correct answer: Which of the following is correct?
A: In software engineering design phase follows testing phase
B. In the design phase creation of system architecture and data model definition is done

options.A: Both A and B are true and B is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and B are false and B is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but B is false
options.D: A is false but B is true

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Testing follows design, not the other way round. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: ____ is NOT among the eight principles followed by software code of Ethics.
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: ACM/IEEE-CS code: Public, Client and Employer, Product, Judgment, Management, Profession, Colleagues, Self. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: Pressman's generic process framework consists of which five framework activities?
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Inception…production are Unified Process phases; Sommerville's four activities are specification, development, validation, evolution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an umbrella activity in the generic process framework?
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Umbrella activities span the whole project: tracking, risk management, SQA, technical reviews, measurement, SCM, reusability management, work-product preparation.

questions.question: In Pressman's layered view of software engineering, the 'bedrock' and the 'foundation' are respectively:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Layers bottom-up: quality focus → process → methods → tools.

questions.question: A 'task set' in a software process is:

options.C: The schedule chart of the project
options.D: The collection of work tasks, work products, quality assurance points and milestones for a framework action

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Different projects choose different task sets for the same action (e.g. requirements gathering).

questions.question: A process pattern describes:

options.B: A process-related problem met during software work, its environment and a proven solution

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Ambler's process patterns are of three types: stage, task and phase patterns.

questions.question:
Match the process flows with their descriptions:
a. Linear
b. Iterative
c. Evolutionary
d. Parallel

1. Activities executed in a circular manner, each circuit giving a more complete version
2. Repeats one or more activities before moving to the next
3. Each framework activity executed once in sequence
4. Executes one or more activities alongside others
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Pressman, chapter 2.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Software does not 'wear out' the way hardware does.
Reason (R): Software is not susceptible to the environmental maladies (dust, heat, vibration) that cause hardware to wear out.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Software deteriorates because of change (side-effects of modifications), giving the 'actual' failure curve with spikes.

questions.question: The CMMI maturity level at which processes are measured and controlled using statistical and quantitative techniques is:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Levels: 1 Initial, 2 Managed, 3 Defined, 4 Quantitatively Managed, 5 Optimizing (continuous improvement).

questions.question:
Match the process assessment approaches:
a. SCAMPI
b. SPICE
c. ISO 9001:2000
d. CBA IPI

1. ISO/IEC 15504 standard
2. Generic quality-management standard
3. SEI's five-step assessment model for CMMI
4. SEI's diagnostic for process maturity
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Standard CMMI-Based Appraisal Method for Process Improvement = SCAMPI.

questions.question: The Personal Software Process (PSP) and the Team Software Process (TSP) were proposed by:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PSP framework activities: planning, high-level design, HLD review, development, postmortem.

questions.question: Modifying software so that it continues to work after the operating system is upgraded is an example of:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Corrective – fix bugs; perfective – new features/performance; preventive – improve future maintainability (re-engineering).

questions.question: The term 'software engineering' was popularised at the 1968 conference organised by:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: It responded to the 'software crisis' – late, over-budget, unreliable software.

questions.question: IEEE defines software engineering as:

options.C: Writing code in a high-level language
options.D: The application of a systematic, disciplined, quantifiable approach to the development, operation and maintenance of software

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: IEEE Std 610.12.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The waterfall model is also called the classic life cycle.
II. The waterfall model suits projects whose requirements keep changing.
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Only I: waterfall needs stable, well-understood requirements; changing requirements suit incremental or agile models.

questions.question: A throwaway prototype differs from an evolutionary prototype in that it:

options.B: Is discarded once requirements are understood

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Prototyping can be used within any process model to clarify fuzzy requirements.

questions.question: Lehman's first law of software evolution, the law of 'continuing change', states that:

options.A: A program used in a real-world environment must change or become progressively less useful

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Lehman's laws apply to E-type (real-world) systems.

questions.question: Brooks' law states that:

options.A: Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later
options.B: 80% of effort goes into 20% of the code
options.C: Software size doubles every two years
options.D: Testing can show only the presence of bugs

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Fred Brooks, The Mythical Man-Month (1975); he also wrote 'No Silver Bullet' (1986).

questions.question: The 'deployment' framework activity includes:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Construction = code generation + testing; planning = estimates, schedule, risks.

questions.question: According to Pressman, software consists of:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Programs that give function, data structures that let programs manipulate information, and documents that describe them.

questions.question: Which statement about legacy software is correct?

options.A: It refers to open-source software only
options.C: It is older software that is often business-critical and may need adaptation, enhancement or re-engineering
options.D: It is always discarded on upgrade

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Legacy systems evolve to meet new environments, requirements and interoperability.

questions.question: The software failure-rate curve of Pressman shows that, unlike hardware, software:

options.B: Fails more as it ages because of dust and heat
options.D: Has no wear-out phase, but failure rate spikes after each change

questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The hardware curve is the 'bathtub curve' (infant mortality, wear out).

questions.question: 'A general statement of objectives is sufficient to begin writing programs – we can fill in the details later.' This is a:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Practitioner myth: 'once the program works, our job is done'; management myth: 'if we fall behind, we can add more programmers'.

questions.question: In a feasibility study, checking whether the organisation's staff and users will accept and use the proposed system is:
questions.subject: Software Process, Generic Process Model and the Life Cycle
questions.explanation: Technical – can it be built; economic – cost–benefit; schedule – can it be done in time.

sets.name: 2 · Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management

questions.question:
Match the following and choose the correct answer
a. Waterfall model  b. Agile model  c. Iterative model  d. V model
i. Emphasises flexibility and customer satisfaction  ii. Sequential design process  iii. Validation and verification  iv. Repeated cycle

options.A: a – iv, b – iii, c – ii, d – i
options.B: a – ii, b – i, c – iv, d – iii
options.C: a – iii, b – i, c – iv, d – ii
options.D: a – iii, b – iv, c – ii, d – i

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Waterfall – sequential; agile – flexibility; iterative – repeated cycles; V-model – verification and validation. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question:
Arrange the component-based development process activities in the correct order:
a. Requirement analysis
b. Component qualification
c. System design with reuse
d. Component adaptation
e. Component composition
f. Component discovery
g. System integration and testing

options.A: f, a, b, c, d, g, e
options.B: a, c, f, b, d, e, g
options.C: b, a, f, c, d, e, g
options.D: a, f, c, b, d, g, e

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Requirements first, then architectural design with reuse, then find, qualify, adapt and compose components, and finally integrate and test. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In a spiral model cycle, the probability of failure for each iteration due to risk is 10%. If there are 4 cycles, then what is the probability that the project completes all cycles without failure?
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: 0.9⁴ = 0.6561. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: How to estimate the effort using cost per person-month to calculate total cost of a software, if it has 10 persons-months and the average cost per person-month as $5000. The total cost is:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: 10 person-months × $5,000 = $50,000. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A software is requiring 5000 Lines (LoC). Using basic COCOMO model, the effort E is calculated as E = 3 × (KLoC)^1.2. With these details, derive the estimated effort rightly in person-months.
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: 5000 LoC = 5 KLoC, so E = 3 × 5^1.2 ≈ 20.7 person-months. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The ____ is a dynamic multivariable model that assumes a specific distribution of effort over the life of a software development project.
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Putnam's software equation is the dynamic multivariable model described in Pressman. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ approach is used when a project encompasses the use of existing software that must be modified in some way as part of a project
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Change sizing estimates the modifications (reuse, adding, changing, deleting code) made to existing software. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Assume a software team applies COCOMO II Early Design Model. If the system is later migrated to a cloud-native microservices architecture, then which cost driver becomes the most volatile and error-prone in recalculating effort?
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Changing the underlying platform is what platform volatility measures. (Strictly, PVOL belongs to the Post-Architecture model; this is the intended answer.) (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In Pressman's V-model, which pair of a development activity and its testing activity is correct?
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Requirements ↔ acceptance; architectural design ↔ system testing; component design ↔ integration testing; code ↔ unit testing.

questions.question: In the incremental model, the first increment is usually:

options.A: A core product addressing basic requirements

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Each later increment adds features based on the customer's evaluation.

questions.question: In Boehm's spiral model, the radial dimension represents:

options.C: The cumulative cost incurred so far

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each loop has four quadrants: determine objectives, identify and resolve risks, develop and test, plan the next iteration.

questions.question: The Rapid Application Development (RAD) model is suitable when:

options.A: The system is safety-critical and novel
options.D: Requirements are well understood, scope is constrained and reusable components exist (60–90 day cycles)

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: RAD is a high-speed incremental model relying on component reuse.

questions.question: In the concurrent development model, all software engineering activities:

options.C: Exist concurrently but reside in different states (e.g. under development, awaiting changes, done)

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: It is represented as a series of framework activities with state transitions triggered by events.

questions.question: Cleanroom software engineering is an example of:

options.C: Formal methods – mathematical specification and correctness verification

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Formal specification languages include Z and VDM; formal methods are costly but suit safety-critical systems.

questions.question: Aspect-oriented software development (AOSD) addresses:

options.B: Crosscutting concerns such as security, logging and transaction handling

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). An 'aspect' captures a concern that cuts across many components.

questions.question: In the Unified Process, the phase that establishes an executable architectural baseline and refines use cases is:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Inception – business case; construction – build; transition – beta and delivery; production – operation.

questions.question: The four Ps of effective software project management are:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: People are listed first as the most important factor.

questions.question: Boehm's W5HH principle asks questions such as:

options.A: Who pays, who uses, who tests?
options.B: Why is the system being developed? What will be done? When? Who is responsible? Where are they? How will it be done? How much is needed?
options.C: What tests, what tools, what reports?
options.D: Which language, which compiler, which hardware?

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It gives a project plan outline for small and large projects.

questions.question: Using basic COCOMO for an organic project of 32 KLOC (E = 2.4 × KLOC^1.05), the estimated effort is about:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management

questions.question: The unadjusted function point count of a system is 300 and the sum of the 14 value adjustment factors is 45. The adjusted FP is:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). FP = UFP × [0.65 + 0.01 × ΣFi] = 300 × 1.10 = 330.

questions.question: A risk has a 60% probability of occurring and would cost ₹50,000 if it occurs. Its risk exposure is:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: RE = P × C = 0.6 × 50,000. Risks are handled through an RMMM (mitigation, monitoring, management) plan.

questions.question: Tasks: A (3 days) precedes B (4 days) and C (6 days); B and C both precede D (2 days). The length of the critical path is:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Paths: A-B-D = 9, A-C-D = 11. The critical path is the longest path; its tasks have zero slack.

questions.question: If BCWP (earned value) = 40 and BCWS (planned value) = 50, the schedule performance index (SPI) is:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: SPI = BCWP/BCWS; CPI = BCWP/ACWP. Values below 1 mean behind schedule / over budget.

questions.question: COCOMO II's Application Composition model sizes software using:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: The Early Design and Post-Architecture models use function points or KLOC.

questions.question: Putnam's software equation is derived from the:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Effort = [LOC × B^0.333 / P]³ × (1/t⁴).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The spiral model suits large, high-risk projects.
Reason (R): Every loop of the spiral includes an explicit risk-analysis step.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Risk-driven iteration is the defining feature of the spiral.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The incremental model delivers an operational product with each increment.
II. In the prototyping model the prototype is always delivered as the final product.
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: Only I: prototypes are often thrown away after clarifying requirements.

questions.question: Component-based development (CBD) mainly relies on:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: It follows the evolutionary (spiral-like) approach and focuses on integration.

questions.question: A Gantt chart in project scheduling shows:

options.B: Tasks as horizontal bars against a time line
options.C: The network of task dependencies with probabilistic times
options.D: The flow of data between processes

questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PERT uses three time estimates: te = (o + 4m + p)/6.

questions.question: With PERT, a task with optimistic 2, most likely 4 and pessimistic 12 days has expected time:
questions.subject: Prescriptive and Specialised Process Models, Estimation and Project Management
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). te = (2 + 4×4 + 12)/6 = 30/6 = 5.

sets.name: 1 · Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD

questions.question: What are the phases of the Adaptive Software Development Model?

options.B: Requirements, Analysis, Design, Evolution and Delivery
options.C: Feasibility Study, Business Study, Functional Model Iteration, Design and Build Iteration, Implementation

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: ASD (Highsmith) cycles through speculation, collaboration and learning; option 3 lists the DSDM phases. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Sprint Retrospective in SCRUM FRAMEWORK?

options.A: To plan for another Scrum's Sprint
options.B: To review test cases from the beginning
options.C: To review the past Scrum's Sprint and identify any improvement

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: The retrospective inspects how the last sprint went and plans improvements; sprint planning is a separate event. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the Agile practices with their corresponding principles or benefits:
a. Pair Programming
b. Test-driven Development
c. Continuous Integration
d. Refactoring
(i) Avoids integration issues by validating changes frequently in shared repositories.
(ii) Ensures correctness through automated specification before implementation.
(iii) Facilitates early problem discovery and real-time code review.
(iv) Improves internal code quality without altering external behaviour

options.A: a → i, b → ii, c → iii, d → iv
options.B: a → ii, b → iii, c → iv, d → i
options.C: a → iv, b → i, c → ii, d → iii
options.D: a → iii, b → ii, c → i, d → iv

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: Pair programming = continuous review; TDD = tests first; CI = frequent integration; refactoring = better structure, same behaviour. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which software development model is known for its iterative approach where feedback is gathered after each cycle?
questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: Agile delivers small increments and gathers customer feedback each iteration. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q76

questions.question: How many phases are there in scrum?
questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: KEA's key gives five. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: 3 Cs of user stories do not include this
questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: Ron Jeffries' 3 Cs: Card, Conversation, Confirmation. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four values of the Agile Manifesto (2001)?

options.B: Responding to change over following a plan
options.C: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The real value is 'working software over comprehensive documentation'.

questions.question: The five values of Extreme Programming (XP) are:

options.A: Communication, simplicity, feedback, courage and respect
options.B: Inspect, adapt, review, retrospect and release
options.C: Speculation, collaboration, learning, delivery and review
options.D: Planning, design, coding, testing and deployment

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: XP was proposed by Kent Beck.

questions.question: In XP, a 'spike solution' is:

options.D: An operational prototype built to lower risk on a difficult design problem

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). XP design uses CRC (class-responsibility-collaborator) cards and the KIS (keep it simple) principle.

questions.question: In XP, which practice is followed BEFORE writing the code for a story?

options.B: Developing unit tests for the story (test-first)

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: Unit tests are automated so they can be run repeatedly for regression testing.

questions.question: In pair programming, the two roles are:
questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The driver types; the navigator reviews and thinks strategically; roles switch often.

questions.question: In Scrum, the person responsible for maximising the value of the product and managing the product backlog is the:
questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master is a servant-leader who removes impediments.

questions.question: The maximum length of a sprint in the Scrum Guide is:
questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Typical sprints are two to four weeks; the daily scrum is time-boxed to 15 minutes.

questions.question: The purpose of the Sprint Review is to:

options.C: Inspect the increment with stakeholders and adapt the product backlog

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: Retrospective = improve the process; daily scrum = sync for 24 hours.

questions.question: A team's velocity is 30 story points per sprint and the remaining product backlog is 120 points. About how many sprints are needed?
questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 120 / 30 = 4. A burndown chart plots the remaining work against time.

questions.question: DSDM (Dynamic Systems Development Method) is based on which principle?

options.A: Every feature must take two weeks
options.B: 80 percent of an application can be delivered in 20 percent of the time it would take to deliver the complete application
options.C: Testing is done only at the end
options.D: All requirements must be frozen first

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: DSDM uses MoSCoW prioritisation and phases: feasibility study, business study, functional model iteration, design & build iteration, implementation.

questions.question: In Feature Driven Development (FDD), a feature is:

options.C: A client-valued function that can be implemented in two weeks or less

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). FDD processes: develop an overall model, build a features list, plan by feature, design by feature, build by feature.

questions.question: In Adaptive Software Development, 'speculation' refers to:

options.A: Adaptive cycle planning using the customer's mission statement, project constraints and basic requirements

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: Collaboration uses JAD-style teamwork; learning uses focus groups, technical reviews and postmortems.

questions.question: Kanban as an agile method is characterised by:

options.C: Visualising work on a board and limiting work in progress (WIP)

questions.subject: Agile Manifesto, XP, Scrum, ASD, DSDM and FDD
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It originated in Toyota's lean production system.

questions.question: The Crystal family of agile methods (Alistair Cockburn) is organised by:
